blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence:
Two columns, `birthday` (month and day, no year) and `phone`, are added to `profiles`, filled only for members who opt in. They are
kept as long as the profile exists, and copied with the rest of the
database into the nightly backups.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: Tie retention to the purpose (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), storage limitation): clear `birthday` and `phone` when the member opts out, and state how long the nightly backups keep them (backup rotation period) so a purged value disappears from backups within a defined delay. Add a spec scenario "A member opts out → birthday and phone are erased from the profile" and a matching task. Scenario that fails today: a member opts in, later turns greetings off; their birth date and mobile number stay in `profiles` for the life of the account and in every backup indefinitely, with no purpose left.
findings.title: Birthday and phone kept after opt-out and in backups with no expiry

findings.evidence: The profile form SHALL offer birthday greetings as an option, off by default; a member who opts in SHALL give their birthday (day and month) and a mobile phone number.
findings.location: specs/birthday-greetings/spec.md#Requirement: Members opt in to birthday greetings
findings.recommendation: Add a requirement that a member can withdraw (opt out) at any time and that withdrawal stops the messages (Art. 7(3), Art. 21 for direct marketing), and confirm that access, rectification, erasure and portability (Art. 15–20) cover `birthday` and `phone`. Confidence low: the repository shows no existing export or account-deletion path to check whether it would reach the new columns.
findings.title: Opt-out and data-subject rights not specified for the new fields

findings.evidence:
A daily job selects the profiles whose birthday is today and posts each
phone number and display name to Textly's API (hosted in the United
States), which sends the message.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: Textly is a new processor receiving mobile numbers and display names, and the transfer goes outside the EEA (GDPR Art. 28, Chapter V). State in the design the processor agreement and the transfer mechanism (adequacy decision / Data Privacy Framework certification, or SCCs), Textly's retention of the numbers and message content, and record it in the records of processing (Art. 30). Confidence low: only the controller knows whether a DPA and safeguards are in place.
findings.title: Phone numbers and names sent to a US processor without a stated transfer safeguard

findings.evidence: Members enjoy being remembered; marketing wants birthday messages.
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: state the purpose (member greeting vs. marketing) and the lawful basis (consent via the opt-in, presumably) for `birthday` and `phone` (Art. 5(1)(b), Art. 6). If the messages are marketing, the SMS channel also needs prior consent under the ePrivacy rules, and the opt-in wording must say so; the phone number must not be reused for other campaigns without a new basis.
findings.title: Purpose and lawful basis of the new data not stated
